title: Marjorie Estiano and Any Gabrielly Fight for Justice and Redress: 'Habeas Corpus,' Netflix Brazil's First Legal Drama, Premiering September 23
summary: Netflix Brazil has just released the trailer for Habeas Corpus, its first legal drama, starring Marjorie Estiano and Any Gabrielly.
body_markdown:
São Paulo, September 1, 2026 -


Netflix Brazil has just released the trailer for


Habeas Corpus


, its first legal drama, starring


Marjorie Estiano


and


Any Gabrielly


. The trailer offers a glimpse of what viewers can expect over the course of the eight episodes premiering on


September 23


— a story that blends courtroom tension with touches of melodrama and complex personal relationships, tied together by the pursuit of justice and redress. In the trailer, we see Inez (Marjorie Estiano), a lawyer and former criminal defense attorney, bring together a group of students to revisit the case of a young man who may have been wrongfully convicted. Her efforts are driven by one of the central questions at the heart of the story: does everyone truly have equal access to justice? Among the students is Marina (Any Gabrielly), whose connection to the case — and to Inez herself — runs much deeper than it first appears, concealing a personal agenda rooted in an injustice from the past. As the group searches for answers, secrets come to light and long-held assumptions begin to unravel. Gradually, the investigation reveals that delivering justice in the present will mean confronting the truths of the past. Directed by Luiz Villaça, who also created the series with Leonardo Moreira and Donna Oliveira,


Habeas Corpus


is produced by Café Royal, with Adriana Tavares serving as executive producer. Episodes are directed by Villaça and Flávia Lacerda. The screenplay, written by Leonardo Moreira, is inspired by real cases and by the work of the Innocence Project Brasil, an organization that investigates and helps to overturn wrongful convictions in the country. The cast also includes


Felipe Ricca


,


Hypólito


,


Luiza Gabus


,


Naruna Costa


,


Nicolas Lee


,


Paula Cohen


,


Pedro Roza, Renata Gaspar


and


Tato Gabus Mendes.


About Café Royal


Café Royal is an entertainment and advertising production company known for its creative, collaborative approach and commitment to social impact, working across film, documentaries, series and theater. Led by Adriana Tavares, Luiz Villaça, Julio Hey and Moa Ramalho, the company is currently finishing up the documentary


Mulheres Crônicas


, featuring Tati Bernardi, for Aquarius, and beginning production on the feature film


The Last Chance


, about basketball players Paula and Hortência. Its film credits include


45 do Segundo Tempo


, directed by Luiz Villaça and starring Tony Ramos, as well as


Angicos


, a project about the life of Paulo Freire, developed by the company and directed by Felipe Hirsch. Its documentary work includes


From Love No One Escapes


and


Samadhi Road


, by the Ahimsa brothers, as well as


Homeland Is the Place Where We Are Loved


, directed by Felipe Hirsch, in partnership with Sesc and the Museu da Língua Portuguesa and


Radical Love


, directed by Julio Hey and produced by Aquarius, about the life and legacy of Satish Kumar. The company is also completing a documentary about the play


Eu de Você


, starring Denise Fraga. For television, it produced the series


Justiça por Elas


, for GNT, and in theater it co-produced the plays


Eu de Você


, starring Denise Fraga and


O Que Só Sabemos Juntos


, starring Denise Fraga and Tony Ramos.
